subject: SDK connection recovery: proposed guidance for streaming reconnects and idempotency
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@helixpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDK connection recovery: impact seen during HelixPay POC

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary and the ask from our side: during your POC run you saw a streaming session reconnect that produced duplicated partial outputs and an out-of-order finalization event. You sent over the small log excerpt (attached) which shows two reconnects for request id rp_8a9c within ~350ms and both resumed producing tokens.

We'd like to propose a short cross-functional checklist so Sales Eng / Field can give Helix a clear recommendation that balances compatibility and safety: 
- Immediate: ask Helix to use an idempotency key per logical generation (they can reuse the same key across reconnects)
- Near-term SDK change: expose an explicit "X-Redwood-Resume-Token" header in SDK reconnect flow so client-side can assert resume semantics
- Runtime fallback: server-side de-dup based on (request-id + resume-seq) when resume token absent

Can the runtime/SDK teams weigh in with feasibility and rough ETA? If we can commit to a concrete plan we can avoid Helix pausing their pilot. I'm looping Karthik and Marissa to coordinate the recommended wording.

Attachments: helixpay-streaming-log-snippet.txt (text), poc-architecture-diagram.png (image)

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0147

From: Alex Moreno <alex@helixpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelixPay POC <poc@helixpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK connection recovery: impact seen during HelixPay POC

Sean — appreciate the summary. Confirming the behavior we saw: two reconnects after a transient network blip, both resumed and produced overlapping token sequences; app-level dedupe is tricky because tokens are partial and not easily comparable. 

We can surface an idempotency key from our side (we already have a request GUID per user query), but we can't change the SDK in our stack quickly. A header option in the Redwood SDK would be ideal. Short-term we can gate streaming on a small client retry window so we don't display duplicates, but that's brittle.

Happy to join a quick sync with your runtime folks — we need a clear short-term mitigation (1–2 days) and a roadmap item for a proper SDK resume contract (2–3 sprints).

— Alex
Alex Moreno
Director, Engineering (Integrations), HelixPay
alex@helixpay.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK connection recovery: impact seen during HelixPay POC

Team — quick technical read:
- Runtime: we can add a server-side best-effort de-dup when we see duplicate resume ranges for the same request-id. That is low-risk but won't cover cases where client reconnects with a different request id.
- SDK: exposing a resume token header in the SDK reconnect handshake is straightforward in the JS/TS and Python SDKs (1 sprint) and requires a clear contract (how resume offsets are represented).
- Backcompat: must default to current behavior so existing customers are not broken. We should gate the resume header with an opt-in flag and document it as experimental.

Action proposals: 
1) Short-term (next 48h): runtime team adds heuristic de-dup logs + mitigation switch we can enable per-customer. Dev, can you sketch the flag and a couple of fallback heuristics?
2) Mid-term (2 sprints): SDK exposes resume token header + new tests for partial-token reassembly.

Dev — tagging you for feasibility and a quick rough ETA. Marissa/Sean — if you can push the short-term mitigation as 'enable for HelixPay' that buys us runway.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Platform/Runtime

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Moreno <alex@helixpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK connection recovery: impact seen during HelixPay POC

All — quick status and proposed implementation details: 

Short-term (today -> 48h):
- Added an experimental per-customer flag runtime.resume_dedupe.enabled that enables server-side dedupe for overlapping resume windows for the same request-id. The flag also turns on verbose resume diagnostics in traces. We can enable it for HelixPay immediately.
- The mitigation uses a conservative threshold: if two resume sessions overlap by >= 50 tokens within 500ms, the runtime will suppress the later tokens at the stream boundary and emit a resume-warning telemetry event.

Mid-term (2 sprints):
- SDK: expose optional resume token on reconnect handshake (header X-Redwood-Resume-Token). Tokens will be {request_id}:{resume_offset}. SDKs will default to not sending the header to preserve backcompat; we'll add an opt-in flag in SDK ctor (resumePolicy: 'disabled'|'opt-in'|'strict').
- Runtime: add idempotency reconciliation logic that prefers the earlier stream unless client explicitly sends resume token that maps to a newer offset.

Tests and rollout plan:
- I'll push a small runtime patch to staging today and coordinate a release toggle for HelixPay. Karthik/Marissa — please confirm we can flip the flag for HP-3247 and that Sales Eng will notify the Helix engineering team with the exact toggle name.

Notes: this approach minimizes breaking changes and gives the field a clear short-term stopgap while we ship the SDK contract. Attached is a quick patch summary (pseudocode) and the log snippet analysis.

-dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai
